blindSourceSummaries: An international human-rights organisation's statement (26 March 2026) on the country's 2026 trans-rights amendment bill passed by parliament: removes self-identification, restricts recognition to culturally recognised third-gender and intersex categories, mandates medical certification, and creates offences carrying up to life imprisonment for 'coercing or alluring' someone to be transgender. National framework applying uniformly in this state/province; no local reporting.

A foreign broadcaster (26 March 2026): the amendment removing self-identification passed both houses amid protests, adds mandatory medical-board certification for gender-affirming surgery, drew a withdrawal request from the country's highest court-appointed advisory panel, and awaits presidential assent. Applies nationally including this state/province; the piece has no regional angle.

A national daily (18 August 2024): alleged 'gender check' groping of a trans person by a railway security-force constable at a metro station, denied by the force with a counter-complaint. An incident in another state/province kept here as a national datapoint on security-forces screening of gender-nonconforming people, not a local finding.
